```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<robot name="chest_with_lid">
  <!-- Dimensions (metres) -->
  <!-- Chest footprint: 1.06 (X width) x 0.35 (Y depth) -->
  <!-- Chest interior height: 0.20 (assumed to correspond to outer height) -->

  <material name="wood">
    <color rgba="0.55 0.33 0.20 1.0"/>
  </material>
  <material name="wood_dark">
    <color rgba="0.35 0.22 0.14 1.0"/>
  </material>
  <material name="metal">
    <color rgba="0.65 0.65 0.7 1.0"/>
  </material>

  <!-- World root -->
  <link name="world"/>

  <!-- Parameters used in URDF:
       Width (X): 1.06 -> half = 0.53
       Depth (Y): 0.35 -> half = 0.175
       Height (Z): 0.20 -> top at Z=0.20
       We'll model a shell thickness for sides/bottom/lid: 0.02 m
       We'll place origin on the floor at the center of the object (X=0, Y=0 mid-depth, Z=0).
       Front faces -Y, so "back edge" is +Y. -->

  <!-- Chest body (base) -->
  <link name="chest_body">
    <inertial>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.10"/>
      <!-- Approximate as composite box; tuned to a plausible wooden mass -->
      <mass value="18.0"/>
      <!-- Inertia for a rectangular prism (approx outer 1.06 x 0.35 x 0.20),
           using Ixx=1/12*m*(y^2+z^2), Iyy=1/12*m*(x^2+z^2), Izz=1/12*m*(x^2+y^2) -->
      <inertia ixx="0.206533" iyy="1.639467" izz="1.667333" ixy="0" ixz="0" iyz="0"/>
    </inertial>

    <!-- Collision geometry: outer shell approximated by a single solid box -->
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.10" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="1.06 0.35 0.20"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="wood"/>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.10" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="1.06 0.35 0.20"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Lid -->
  <link name="chest_lid">
    <inertial>
      <!-- Lid thickness 0.02, lid is at Z=0.20 (top surface) - but center of lid box at Z=0.20 - 0.01 -->
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.19"/>
      <!-- Approximate lid as a flat plate: box 1.06 x 0.35 x 0.02 -->
      <mass value="4.5"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.001706" iyy="0.03645" izz="0.03645" ixy="0" ixz="0" iyz="0"/>
    </inertial>

    <!-- Visual -->
    <visual>
      <!-- Lid is rotated about back edge at +Y, centered in X, spans full depth. -->
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.19" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="1.06 0.35 0.02"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="wood_dark"/>
    </visual>

    <!-- Collision -->
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.19" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="1.06 0.35 0.02"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>

    <!-- Simple hinge leaves (purely for collision/visual; still real mass/inertia) -->
    <gazebo reference="chest_lid">
      <!-- not used -->
    </gazebo>
  </link>

  <!-- Joint between body and lid -->
  <!-- Hinged along the back edge (+Y). Lid swings up.
       Choose joint axis along X (width), so rotation happens in the Y-Z plane: hinged at back edge.
       Joint frame located at the back edge and at the lid's bottom surface? We'll set hinge at Z=0.20 and Y=+0.175.
       Lid currently has its box centered at Z=0.19 (thickness 0.02), so bottom surface at Z=0.18.
       To make hinge at the back edge along its "back edge line", we set joint origin at:
         x=0, y=+0.175, z=0.18 (lid bottom surface)
       The lid box is centered at z=0.19 so bottom is z=0.18.
       Rotate around +X. Use rpy to align axis with URDF axis: axis=(1,0,0). -->
  <joint name="lid_hinge" type="revolute">
    <parent link="chest_body"/>
    <child link="chest_lid"/>
    <origin xyz="0 0.175 0.18" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <axis xyz="1 0 0"/>
    <limit lower="0" upper="1.57079632679" effort="50" velocity="1.5"/>
    <dynamics damping="0.2" friction="0.05"/>
  </joint>

  <!-- Attach world to chest_body for convenience -->
  <joint name="world_to_chest_body" type="fixed">
    <parent link="world"/>
    <child link="chest_body"/>
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
  </joint>
</robot>
```
